title: Stop requests whose entry mode contradicts their card data

blocks.text: Your gateway sits between a few hundred terminals of different makes and the acquirer. The acquirer's fraud team has written to you: some of your requests say one thing in field 22 and another in the card fields after it, and they want those stopped at the gateway, answered with response code 30, instead of reaching their host. The first example they attached is a chip read with no chip data. It is not the only kind.

`EntryModeScreen.screen` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/EntryModeScreen.java` already answers the terminal when there is a problem. Finish `problem(...)`, marked `TODO`, so that it finds every request whose read and card data disagree, and only those. The codes the acquirer's specification lists are constants at the top of the class. Your terminals are not all alike: some have a PIN pad and some don't.

cases.says: a chip read that carries a track and chip data goes upstream
a keyed card that carries its expiry date goes upstream
a request that claims a chip read but carries no chip data is answered at the gateway with response code 30
the third digit of field 22 describes the terminal, not the read, so a terminal without a PIN pad is not refused
a contactless chip read needs chip data just like a contact chip read
a keyed card that also carries track 2 contradicts itself: a field the read cannot produce is a problem too
an entry mode the acquirer's specification does not list is refused rather than passed on

origin.section: 5.3 How the Card Was Read Decides the Card Fields

concepts: Field 22 and the card fields 14, 35 and 55 come from one value describing how the card was read, so a request never claims a read its data contradicts.
